topic: How do GEO and LEO orbital altitudes impact link budget calculations for Ka vs S-band deployments in 5G satcom?
consensus_response: The varying orbital altitudes significantly impact link budget calculations due to differences in signal propagation characteristics. In Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO), increased atmospheric absorption affects Ka-band signals more significantly than S-band, reducing the link budget by 10-15 dB. Conversely, Low Earth Orbit (LEO) constellations experience less atmospheric interference but higher ionospheric effects on Ka-band frequencies. The reduced signal propagation delay in LEO enables faster data transmission for S-band frequencies, increasing reliability. However, this also means that the signal has less time to propagate through the atmosphere, leading to increased atmospheric losses for Ka-band frequencies.
reference_context: Satellite communications in 5G networks involve integrating satellite and terrestrial networks, with satellite constellations deployed in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) providing global coverage and reduced propagation delays. LEO constellations can support massive machine-type communications, enhanced mobile broadband, and ultra-reliable communications with high availability.
